summary: Brooke Schedneck specializes in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Arizona State University, where she studied under doctoral supervisor Juliane Schober.

Bruce B. Lawrence (born 1941) is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. Educated at Fay School, Princeton University, and Episcopal Divinity School, he served at Duke University as Professor (~1971–2011) and later as Distinguished Professor Emeritus of Religion.

Bruce Cameron Hall works in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He earned his PhD from Harvard University in 1980 and served as assistant editor at the College of William & Mary (attested 1987).
Bruce Charles Williams works in sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Edward H. Schafer, Michael C. Rogers, Michel Strickmann, Barend A. van Nooten, Padmanabh S. Jaini, and Akira Fujieda.
Bruce Chilton (born 1949) is a religious studies scholar who studied at St John's College (~1974–1977). He held posts at Yale University (~1985–1987) and served as director at Bard College (~1987).

Bruce John Stewart specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Sakya College and earned his PhD at Columbia University (attested 1983) under Alex Wayman, also studying under Joel Peter Brereton and Christopher S. George.

Bruce Kapferer (born 1940) studied at the University of Sydney and University of Manchester. A religious studies scholar, he held posts at Adelaide, University College London, Bergen, James Cook University, and the University of Gothenburg.

Bruce Lincoln (born 1948) works in religious studies, history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Haverford and the University of Chicago under Mircea Eliade, later holding professorships at Minnesota and Chicago.
Bruce M. Knauft (born 1954) studied at the University of Michigan (~1976–1983). In ~1985, he became the Samuel C. Dobbs Professor of Anthropology at Emory University.
Bruce M. Sullivan (born 1951) is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He studied under J. A. B. van Buitenen (~1973–1979) and held a post at Northern Arizona University in ~1989.

Bruce Matthews (born 1941) specializes in religious and Buddhist studies. After graduate studies at McMaster University (~1969–1974), he held posts at the University of Ceylon (~1970–1971) and Acadia University (~1976–2006) as Professor of Comparative Religion.

Bruce McCoy Owens works in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He held a post at Columbia University (attested 1988) and has served as associate professor of anthropology at Wheaton College (attested 2019).

Bruno Dagens (1935–2023) was an Indology and archaeology scholar who studied under Colette Caillat. He held posts at the EFEO, KU Leuven, the French Institute of Pondicherry, and Sorbonne Nouvelle University as professor of ancient history and archaeology.
Bruno Galasek specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Bonn under the supervision of Konrad Klaus (attested 2016).

Bruno Liebich (1862–1939) was an Indologist who studied at Munich, Göttingen, and Breslau, learning under Franz Kielhorn. He held academic posts at the University of Breslau (attested 1902; 1921–1928) and Heidelberg University (attested 1918).

Bruno Lindner (1853–1930) worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig and under Rudolf von Roth, later serving as Privatdocent at Leipzig from 1878 to 1919.

Bruno Petzold (1873–1949) studied at Leipzig, Berlin, and under Hikoshiro Hoshino and Daito Shimaji. A Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar, he taught at the First Higher School (1917–1943), Chuo University, Rissho University, and Seikei High School.

Bruno Schindler (1882–1964) was a Sinologist who completed his doctorate under August Conrady, founded the journal Asia Major in 1923, and worked as a publisher's editor at Lund Humphries (~1939–1964).

Bryan D. Lowe is a scholar of religious, Buddhist, and Japanese studies who studied at Otani University and under Jacqueline I. Stone. He served as Assistant Professor of Religious Studies at Vanderbilt University (attested 2017–2019).

Bryan J. Cuevas studied at Emory and the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano. A Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar, he held a fellowship at Princeton and became John F. Priest Professor of Religion at Florida State University.
